steps.content: Night falls, and the club becomes a honeyed trap. A veneer of glamour enshrouds the entire cruise ship, masking the scent of damp and decay.

It isn't a performance night for Sallie or Milly, but they've dressed up anyway, not in their flashy stage costumes, but in understated, tasteful clothes that let them blend into the circles of money and power, to uncover a story that isn't theirs to tell.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Come on, smile. Don't be so tense.
Milly smooths the ends of Sallie's hair and whispers in her ear.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: With that look on your face, you won't get a word of truth out of those people.
Sallie nods and takes a deep breath. She tries to mimic Milly, smoothing away the tension in her brow and forcing a stiff smile that she pins to her face like a mask.

The dance floor swirls like a golden tide, swallowing the line between desire and indifference. Milly glides toward a middle-aged man drinking alone at the edge of the floor. He's wearing an impeccably tailored navy suit, the collar embroidered in gold thread with the crest of some old aristocratic merchant guild.
The moment their eyes meet, Milly's face lights up with an innocent, radiant smile. She lets her gaze fall to the glass in his hand, feigning the perfect amount of surprise.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Your drink has such an unusual color... blue like the deep sea, but with light shining through... I've never seen such a beautiful cocktail. What's it called?
Her approach is a bit abrupt, but the patrons here have always welcomed attention from the Jewel of Euphoria. The man smiles, casual and nonchalant.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: You'll have to ask that fellow. He's the one who made it. The color's just for show, but the taste... well, it's not bad. That guy's got some skill.
He jerks his chin toward the bar, his tone offhand, like he's praising a well-trained pet.
Milly follows his gaze.

Cassian stands behind the bar, his sharp profile outlined by the light refracting through a glass. His movements are steady and graceful. Lifting a glass, pouring a drink, giving a firm shake... every motion is a pleasure to watch.

He wears a charming, proper smile and says something that makes a wealthy lady giggle. He leans down to light her cigarette with attentive care, nothing like the silent, weary young man from the other day.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Who is he, anyway? With skills like that, he must be a pretty famous bartender, right?
Milly looks back at the man and asks with feigned curiosity. But the man scoffs like he's heard something absurd. He shakes his head, eyes glinting with undisguised ridicule.

steps.speaker: Guest A
steps.content: Him? Oh, he's famous alright. Just not for mixing drinks. In our circles, he's famous for being a joke.
Meanwhile, Sallie is striking up a conversation with a lady dripping in jewels. The woman takes a sip of her drink, her tone airy.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: Who in our circle doesn't know about his family? They squeezed their way into high society with some special permit. Enjoyed the spotlight for barely two years, and then... pop! The whole family was gone. I heard they were at a party one night, and by the next day, they were either in prison or dead. Like something out of a play. What a fall from grace.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: But why would...
Sallie is at a loss for words, until another woman pipes in, her face dripping with contempt and mockery.

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: What else could it be? His family were pawns put on the board by Falke himself. They were dead from the start. You didn't really think they earned all that fame on their own, did you? What a joke.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: I... I see.

Sallie is still processing what she's just heard. To hide her shock and revulsion, she lowers her gaze and takes a sip of her drink. The lady, however, mistakes this for being awed by the ruthless efficiency of the power struggle, and her voice grows more smug.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: That's right. Mr. Falke pulls all the strings in Eastside. To put it nicely, that little upstart family was a necessary sacrifice for some scheme. To put it bluntly, they were scapegoats on the chopping block. When the axe would fall was entirely up to Falke.

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: But the funny thing is, they really thought they'd made it into high society! Prancing around at parties, putting on their aristocratic airs. It was hilarious.

Sallie presses her lips together and says nothing. The harsh laughter rings in her ears. She looks down and pretends to smooth out her dress, trying to hide the fury in her eyes. She doesn't want to hear another word. But she remembers one name: Falke.
She quickly excuses herself and slips back into the crowd, but she can't help but glance back.

Cassian is still standing behind the bar, his back perfectly straight, like a bronze pillar that's been tarnished but never bent. The woman he was serving turns to leave, offhandedly tossing a few large bills onto the counter. They flutter off the edge onto the carpeted floor.
Cassian looks down at them silently, his face unreadable. After a moment, he bends down, gathers the bills one by one, folds them neatly, and puts them in the cash box.
When he looks up again, that perfect smile is back on his face, as if nothing has happened at all. He's already greeting the next customer.

steps.speaker: Guest D
steps.content: Who doesn't know they were nothing but a joke from the start? Don't tell me you've been fooled by his looks too. Are you really taking him for some fallen young lord?

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: He is a very convincing actor. But if you look closely, you can still tell the difference between him and a true member of the upper class, like yourself.
Milly quirks her lips, feigning agreement. The guest nods with satisfaction, like he's found a kindred spirit.

steps.speaker: Guest D
steps.content: Hahaha, right? They were the only ones who had no clue! They thought they were one of us, when really everyone was just waiting to watch them crash and burn.

Whenever Cassian's name comes up, their first reaction is always laughter. Theatrical, contemptuous laughter. They laugh without restraint, like discussing some trivial gossip, or savoring a farce that has run its course.

steps.speaker: Guest E
steps.content: He used to put on quite a show at parties. Pretty, played piano well enough, really stood out at first glance... But you know his type, right? Just there for decoration. Once you're done with the decorating, you toss them out and nobody misses them.
The gilded glasses glint harshly in the light. They chat and laugh merrily, treating someone's downfall as their after-dinner digestif.

steps.speaker: Guest F
steps.content: So, really, it's no surprise he ended up like this. Their kind always falls the hardest, the ones who are coddled their whole lives but never taught their place. Who would ever mistake them for nobility? Don't make me laugh.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: That's true. Nothing escapes your notice when it comes to character.

Sallie inclines her head, forcing down the revulsion as she raises her glass to the noble lords and ladies. Feeling quite pleased with Sallie's flattery, one of the women pats her hand with a titter, as if bestowing upon her some supreme honor.

steps.speaker: Guest E
steps.content: Oh, my. The way you talk, I'd almost think you were one of us.

That evening, Milly and Sallie made their way through groups of guests, catching more fragments of conversation. Some were vague, others deliberately hollow and evasive, but a few gleamed with chilling truth.

At first, they could still plaster on a smile and play along with a flippant laugh. But as the night wore on, the laughter became harder to fake. They could only force their smiles, letting those harsh words cut into their hearts.

On this ship, it makes no difference. Bartender or dancer, man or woman, Sinner or ordinary person... they're all the same. To those pleasure seekers, they are nothing more than faces that can be easily replaced, symbols to be summoned, demeaned, and commanded at will.
Stamp on one, and no one would even bother to see what they'd crushed under their heel.

It isn't until the night is almost over that they get a break. When a tipsy customer slings his arm around Milly's shoulders and starts to brag, she manages to pull the key piece of information from his loosened tongue with her ability:

Falke, who has just concluded district development meetings in Eastside, is boarding the ship in a few days. Mr. E has personally arranged a private banquet for him, along with a luxurious upper-level suite, complete with private access and round-the-clock security. It's one of the most impenetrable areas on the entire Euphoria.

steps.speaker: Tipsy Guest
steps.content: You know, he never dared to come here before. Terrified someone might get the dirt on him. But not anymore. Oh no. He's finally... cleaned out all those annoying little obstacles. No one can get in his way anymore. Tsk, tsk. Mr. Falke can finally let loose and have a real good time!
At dawn, as the last of the revelers disperse, the two return to the backstage lounge with what they've found. Cassian is already there, waiting.
After hearing their report, he merely nods slightly, the corner of his mouth lifting in an almost imperceptible curve.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: ...Thanks.

He still sits perfectly straight. The metallic gleam on his fingers flickers before disappearing into the shadow of his sleeves. Just like the man himself, a master of hiding secrets in the spaces between light and shadow.
After a moment of silence, Sallie finally asks hesitantly.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: Are you... really planning to go through with it? That man... he has so much power...

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I've been waiting for this moment.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: But you're going alone...

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I can handle it.
Cassian's tone is soft, but it isn't the calm of indifference. It's the calm of a man who is forcing madness and hatred deep into his bones, holding himself together with every ounce of his will.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Then at least take this... With it, you can use my ability. Just in case.
Milly pulls a golden lip balm from her pocket and carefully places it in front of Cassian. But he doesn't touch it, only shakes his head.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: Thank you, but I don't need it. I'm already prepared.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: Do you... not trust us?

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: No. This is my business, and it has nothing to do with you. You don't need to be dragged into it.
Without giving them a chance to respond, Cassian continues.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: The message you want me to deliver. Is it ready?

Sallie nods and pulls a handwritten note from her pocket. It contains basic information about someone named <color=#fb9259>Theodore</color> and a brief message for help. She clutches the note as if it's her last hope.

steps.speaker: Sallie
steps.content: Please, find <color=#fb9259>Theodore</color> and get this message to him.

steps.speaker: Cassian
steps.content: I will.

Footsteps come from outside, and the three of them fall silent. Cassian takes the note and rises to leave, the wan yellow lamplight brushing the hem of his shirt. He disappears into the shadows at the end of the corridor. He doesn't look back.
